summary: Two-week window (Oct 16 09:06 to Oct 30 09:05): 20 real messages, 6 'Antonio Veritrade' test messages excluded. The window opened with two structural changes on Oct 16. Mayson announced that the DMCA report would now be folded into a weekly earnings and performance report 'sent in the General chat every Friday', and twelve minutes later Melissa posted the first such report as a file. That is the first written performance document this client has received in 118 days on the books. The Friday report did not go out on Oct 23; Oct 30 was not yet due at window close. On Oct 21 Mayson warned her about system test messages and six arrived that evening (plus one ChatAddUser service event for the test account). Nothing else happened for five days. On Oct 26 Melissa asked for 'a check in call'. Callie answered on Oct 28, 37 minutes after Mica's reel-inspo drop ('Hello, I’m pretty free! When’s best for you?? Xxx'), proposed 2pm EST / 6pm UK for Oct 29, and Melissa agreed, then at 22:39 that night asked to move it to 1 PM EST. After Melissa's 'just following up!' the next morning Callie confirmed in 49 seconds, asking 'Is that 5 for uk time??' (she did the conversion herself; the slots were given in EST only). The Meet link went out at 13:00 Oct 29. Nobody posted after the call; there is no written recap as of window end. What did not happen in two weeks: Mayson's milabrooks rename (committed Oct 11, 19 days, no confirmation, now overdue); any written answer to the Oct 11 '~100 followers' complaint (19 days; the only subsequent ALTR outreach on this account is the call offer); Stephski's confirmation of the Oct 1-14 payment (due Oct 22, she posted nothing in the window) or the six-cycle reconciliation; any word from Derrek (44 days silent); Mica's ~Oct 21 drop (cadence resumed Oct 28). Client asks fell from 4 to 0: all six of her messages are call logistics, and she did not re-raise the rename, the follower drop, the main IG account (129 days open) or her unconfirmed payments in writing. The optimistic read is that she is saving them for the call; the pessimistic read is the pre-exit pattern this book has seen before (complaints unanswered, then asks drop to zero). Churn: three of four exit signals now fire. Owner silent 44d; a results complaint followed by a call offer rather than a written answer; the 90-day rollout promise and 129-day main IG with no written proof. Billing share is 0 of 14 ALTR messages, so signal 4 is off, but only because billing went silent past its own deadline. No invoice or payment in window; the Oct 15-31 invoice is expected ~Nov 1 and no heads-up had appeared by 09:05 Oct 30. Security: no credentials, codes or bank details posted in the window; a Google Meet link (Oct 29, msg 242) was left out of the evidence quotes.

Mayson consolidated DMCA reporting and gave a proactive heads-up about the test messages. Mica's drop came back Oct 28. No credentials were posted. Nothing in the window mentions leaving, another agency, exports or logins. The Oct 29 call is the pivot: if a written recap with owners and dates follows, this recovers; if the chat goes quiet after the call, treat it as the exit conversation.
